When using long division to divide whole numbers, it's often appropriate to round the final answer.

Content:
For instance, let's find the value of [MATH: 58 \div 7,] rounded to the nearest tenth. We start by going through the long division procedure as usual:

Content:
| | | [MATH: \,\, \phantom{0} {\:\phantom{|}} 8 {\, . \,} 2 {\:\phantom{|}} {\color{black}8} \: \ldots] | / | [MATH: 7] | [MATH: \phantom{|}\!\!\!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{5 {\:\phantom{|}} 8 {\, . \,} 0 {\:\phantom{|}} 0}] | / | [MATH: -\!\!\!] | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 6] | | | | / | | | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 0] | | | / | | [MATH: -\!\!\!] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 4] | | | / | | | | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: 0] | | / | | | [MATH: -\!\!\!] | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 6] | | / | | | | | [MATH: 4] | | / | | | | | [MATH: \vdots] | | |
